idiom_name: handler registry keyed by element kind with a default handler (no visitor classes)
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs neither half of the classic structure: dispatch is already dynamic, so the operation becomes a registry - a Map from element constructor to handler plus one fallback handler - and adding an element kind is a new registration while existing handlers stay untouched and nothing is recompiled. That is strictly smaller than a visitor hierarchy with accept methods, and it is the shape JavaScript code actually uses (Map keys are compared by identity, which is exactly right for element kinds). The class-based form still earns its place when a visitor must carry traversal state and third parties must extend an existing operation: the prototype chain gives the inheritance half for free (`class UnionArea extends Area`), and the element probes with `visitor instanceof UnionArea` or a capability field, but then the same default-case discipline as in the classic pattern applies.
pitfalls: Dispatching on constructor misses subclasses and cross-realm objects: a UnionCircle extending Circle finds no Circle entry, so key on a stable tag or walk the prototype chain (Object.getPrototypeOf).
The fallback decides the failure mode: a no-op silently ignores unknown element kinds, the JavaScript equivalent of a forgotten visit overload, so throw or log there unless ignoring is deliberate.
Mutating the handler map at runtime is global state: two libraries registering the same class overwrite each other, and a handler iterating the registry can see entries added mid-traversal.

Prototypes can be replaced at runtime (Object.setPrototypeOf, monkey-patching), so an `instanceof` capability test can change behaviour between calls - prefer an explicit capability field for long-lived visitors.
